text:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty SEV-2 triggered — GPU hotpath pool exhausted in us-east-1; autoscaler failed to add nodes. Queue growth observed, ~25% client requests returning 429s. Paging oncall: @Ryan (oncall).

Ryan (oncall): acked. digging in now. seeing large enqueue on /v1/generate-hotpath queue. any recent deploys?

Julia (sre): no deploys in the last hour from releases channel. autoscaler metrics show repeated scale attempts but target pool stayed at 0->0. error: 'scale_gain negative'.

Ali (infra): grabbing autoscaler logs. looks like the token/credit allocator rejected burst tokens because tiered-rate policy reported mismatch across hotpath vs warmpool.

Maya (eng-runtime): can you paste the logs? i'm curious whether fallback to warmpool was attempted. we should failover to warmpool before queue drains.

Ali (infra): paste:
```
autoscaler: attemptScale(target=hotpath-pool, desired=8) -> rejected: policy_mismatch(tier=gold, allowed=2)
allocator: token_bucket: available=0, window_ms=1000, rate_config_id=rt-764
warmpool: failover_attempted=false
```

Ryan (oncall): that policy_mismatch line looks bad — why would tier config block autoscale? we haven't changed tier policies today.

Julia (sre): digging into config store. found a recent change last night to ratepolicy mapping (PR #4521) that added stricter per-tenant bucket caps for hotpath to avoid noisy neighbor. it seems the new validation is rejecting quick scale actions when queue growth is sudden.

Oliver (support): customer ops already sending inbound alerts. major customer 'AtlasHealth' is observing 50% of requests 429s from EU and US. we need ETA to reduce impact.

Jenn (customer-ops): confirmed. they routed through dedicated capacity but traffic overflowed to hosted and hit the saturated hotpath. raising severity with them.

Ken (pager): oncall history shows we have warm spare GPUs in us-east-2 that should be eligible for cross-region warmpool. is cross-region failover enabled for the gold tier?

Luca (eng-platform): not by default — cross-region warmpool is gated by tier policy. the PR changed the gating check, inadvertently disallowing cross-region failover when token_bucket windows are low.

Maya (eng-runtime): mitigation proposal: 1) temporarily relax tier gating for hotpath to allow warmpool failover 2) increase token_bucket window to allow short-term burst 3) manual scale up of dedicated hotpath pool while autoscaler config is reverted. anyone object?

Ryan (oncall): sounds good. i'll run steps 1 and 2 and coordinate manual scale.

Ali (infra): applying temporary policy override now: `rbac:allow_failover hotpath=true --reason 'incident 2310001234'`

(2 minutes later)
Ali (infra): policy override applied. warmpool failover now allowed.

Maya (eng-runtime): increasing token bucket window: `kv put /config/ratepolicy/rt-764/window_ms=5000` — will give a 5s smoothing to accept burst tokens.

(10 seconds later)
Maya (eng-runtime): changed. note: longer windows increase short-term cost; watch cost dashboards.

Ryan (oncall): manually requesting scale to 6 GPUs on hotpath: `infra-cli scale pool hotpath-pool --count 6 --reason incident-2310001234`

(30s)
Ali (infra): scale request acknowledged by cloud provider, nodes provisioning.

(60s)
IncidentBot: warmpool failover triggered: routed 20% of new requests to us-east-2 warm GPUs.

(2m)
Oliver (support): AtlasHealth reporting decreased 429s to ~12%, still some errors. sending customer note that we are actively scaling and routing.

Julia (sre): queue depth trending down from 18k -> 2.1k. tokenbucket credits showing positive now. autoscaler health check still shows prior failures but manual scale plus policy override restored capacity.

Ken (pager): can we patch the autoscaler to bypass the stricter validation on surge events? if PR #4521 blocks scaling in sudden surges that's a regression.

Luca (eng-platform): agreed. i'll open an emergency revert PR for the gating logic and also add a canary to ensure it doesn't block in the future.

Maya (eng-runtime): temp mitigation summary i'm adding to incident thread: policy override + larger window_ms + manual scale + warmpool routing. needs to be documented as 'hot-mitigation - do not rely long-term'.

Ryan (oncall): marking incident as partially mitigated. will continue to monitor. restoring normal autoscaler behavior only after revert PR merged and validated.

Jenn (customer-ops): sending updated customer comms: we've scaled and routed traffic; continuing to monitor; follow-up postmortem promised.

(30m later)
Julia (sre): traffic returned to normal baseline. queue stabilized < 200. 429s < 0.5% across regions. starting timeline capture for postmortem.

Ryan (oncall): assigning postmortem drive to Maya + Luca + Julia. include: root cause (PR #4521 gating change), why autoscaler didn't fallback, why warmpool gating failed, and a runbook change to test surge behavior for tier policies.

IncidentBot: Incident status -> Monday-bridge scheduled, Sev-2 -> Postmortem required.

Maya (eng-runtime): noted. I'll draft the chronology and mitigation steps, include config diffs.

Oliver (support): will prepare external customer note template.

Jenn (customer-ops): closing customer notification loop once postmortem published.

Ryan (oncall): thanks everyone. leaving handoff to oncall rotation: @Julia (sre) will take follow-up for next 3 hours.

Julia (sre): taking it. will watch dashboards and coordinate rollback PR with Luca.

(End of thread)
